title: Run an untrusted inner puzzle
security_scope: Original teaching fixture for dynamic application (CLVM `a`). It applies an untrusted inner program to an untrusted solution and returns whatever the program returns; an inner failure rejects the spend. It performs no authorization: nothing binds the inner puzzle to an owner, a hash commitment or a signature, so any caller can run any program. That gap is the lesson, not an oversight to patch here. The applied program's cost is charged to the outer puzzle in the VM; the native oracle uses a generous fixed ceiling and reports exhaustion as inconclusive. Finite differential tests are not a termination, cost or compiler-correctness proof.

limitations: The Chialisp and Rue comparisons are authored for the same strict two-argument ABI; they are not a canonical published module.
Rust's reserved `apply` export is admitted by exact signature and implementation fingerprint and lowered to opcode 2; its name grants nothing.
Every proof model rejects programs containing an application; only finite executed cases are recorded.
Programs that would loop until the cost ceiling are deliberately excluded from named cases because exhaustion is an inconclusive resource result.
